A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, Implicit Models: Expressive Power Scales with Test-Time Compute. All 41 pages of v1 and 48 pages of v2, including figures, equations, tables and appendices, support comparison; relocated material can be matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original deblurring, Navier–Stokes and linear-programming experiments, including iteration-wise measurements and comparisons between implicit and explicit models.

after.justification: v2 retains these experiments and adds original evaluations of a pretrained looped transformer on 200 semantic prompt pairs, alongside expanded model-scaling experiments.

M1.justification: The implemented PGD/HQS operators, implicit FNO and LP-GNN architectures and training procedures are retained. Section 3.4 evaluates an existing pretrained looped transformer without reporting modifications. Appendix F explains existing training strategies rather than introducing a new procedure.

E1.justification: Section 3.4 adds language evaluation using 200 prompt pairs differing by one or two words but requiring different semantic contexts. This substantially extends coverage beyond the retained BSDS500 deblurring, steady Navier–Stokes and generated linear-programming tasks.

E2.justification: The explicit DRUNet, PGD/HQS, FNO and GNN comparison methods are retained. Added depth and width variants change model configurations within these methods. The new language study does not introduce a head-to-head comparator.

E3.justification: Deblurring depth configurations change from 1/2/3 blocks to 1/2/4/8/16/32; FNO comparisons add larger depths and a width sweep, with memory failures at the largest configurations. The language study introduces a Levenshtein-distance ratio, geometric-mean aggregation over 200 pairs, and evaluation across recurrent-block counts. Existing task splits and stated training budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The appendices substantially extend the analysis of whether increasing explicit-model capacity closes the performance gap, including a new FNO width analysis. Section 3.4 adds controlled word-substitution sensitivity measurements and an iteration-by-iteration qualitative example in Table 2. The original image, PDE and LP perturbation analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Existing mean ± standard deviation reporting across test samples is retained. Neither version documents repeated-training-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. The new language figure aggregates its task metric geometrically without adding uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: New scaling and language results are added, including language ratios rising from approximately 29.2 at two iterations to 52.5 at sixteen. At retained explicit FNO depths L=6/12, reported errors change from 0.1585/0.1547 to 0.1526/0.1410; implicit FNO remains 0.0785. New 16-block explicit PGD reaches 28.27 dB versus implicit PGD's unchanged 28.21 dB, qualifying the earlier ranking.

T1.justification: v2 removes boundedness from Assumption 2.2 and Theorem 2.5, adds Theorem A.4's construction over overlapping cubes, and extends the necessity proof to unbounded domains. Corollaries 3.7 and 3.9 consequently drop their bounded-subset restrictions. Definition 2.3 still requires bounded domains, leaving an internal inconsistency in the extension.

C1.justification: The central characterization is broadened from locally Lipschitz targets on bounded domains to potentially unbounded domains. The abstract and contribution list also extend the validation claim from three domains to four, including LLM reasoning. The underlying claim that iteration unlocks expressivity without adding parameters remains.

C2.justification: New Appendix F explicitly identifies guaranteed regularity after training as an open problem and develops the tradeoff between uniform contraction and expressivity. Section 3.4 acknowledges difficulties applying the continuous theory to language, then interprets string-distance growth as semantic differentiation. Expanded scaling discussions emphasize diminishing returns and memory limits, while qualifying deblurring performance as comparable to or better than larger explicit models.

D1.justification: v2 identifies the pretrained model used for language evaluation and supplies an access URL for the new semantic-pair dataset. Existing preprocessing, optimizer, hardware and training details are retained in the relocated experimental appendices. Appendix F mostly consolidates and explains already documented training choices.

R1.justification: New Appendix J substantially expands positioning relative to universality, explicit-network approximation, training convergence, generalization, equilibrium neural tangent kernels and shallow-model equivalence. Eleven references are added, including work by Feng and Kolter, Fung and Berkels, and Ling and colleagues. Earlier cited works are retained despite renumbering and bibliographic edits.

P1.justification: The main narrative order and most original prose remain. v2 locally rewrites the introduction and expressivity discussion, adds a proof roadmap and sufficiency/necessity subsections, and introduces dedicated training and contextual discussions. The original experimental appendices F–H become G–I.

P2.justification: v2 adds the language-output Table 2 and Figure 8, splits and expands v1's deblurring Table 2 into Tables 3–4, and expands the FNO presentation into Tables 5–6. Figure 5 replaces input-channel panels with prediction-error maps. The existing image-perturbation figure is retained as Figure 9.

improvement.justification: The larger depth and width comparisons provide stronger tests of an empirical claim already supported in v1, and Appendix F makes the regularity limitation more explicit. These gains are tempered by the new language metric's lack of independent correctness evaluation and the unbounded-domain extension's inconsistency with Definition 2.3. The net improvement is useful but limited.
